verdict.claim: 4D-SCP lowers compute energy per element-frame versus conventional full-state (full_q) and delta processing, without losing the agent's decisions
verdict.resident_surface_decode: HOLDS on the environment for the temporal-only event path (rank 0, last-value hold, event-driven decoder): 2.37827 pJ/ef vs delta 7.70787 and full_q 5.59945 at T=64, with a stream 2.72× smaller than full_q. It FAILS for the byte-optimal path with relations (21.9011 pJ/ef): every source event fans out into accumulator read-modify-writes and a multiply, so relations buy 1.84× fewer bytes for ~9× the decode energy.
verdict.frame_fixtures: FAILS on the single-cell frame fixtures (v0.1, Medicare, B256, B4096): almost every element changes every frame, so event-driven bookkeeping only adds cost
verdict.stream_out_decode: FAILS: when every decoded value must be streamed out each frame, no scp4d-int path beats full_q, which keeps no state
verdict.encode: FAILS vs delta and FAILS vs full_q on the environment (temporal-only path, incl. the shared ingest quantizer): the encoder must still read the hold state for every element of every input frame
verdict.vs_v019_float: integer arithmetic makes the byte-optimal scp4d decode cheaper than the v0.1.9 float estimate on every fixture
verdict.with_offchip_stream: With the stream priced as off-chip (DRAM-class) traffic, the relations path is the cheapest on the environment: fewer bytes outweigh its on-chip cost (labelled scenario)
verdict.low_rank: Keep low-rank OUT of the hardware datapath (host-side option only): in fixed point it stays within eps, but it changes ~80% of elements every frame and costs ~3.6× the decode energy of the rank-0 path for 16% fewer bytes.

system_view_offchip_stream.label: Labelled scenario: stream bytes priced at DRAM 162.5–325 pJ/B (Horowitz 1.3–2.6 nJ per 64-bit access).
